sentences: Proper losses reward probabilistic forecasts for honestly reporting the underlying chance of an outcome.
Different proper losses can have different optimal regret rates, even on the same forecasting sequence.
The source asks whether one online forecasting algorithm can attain the appropriate optimal rate for every proper loss simultaneously, up to constant or logarithmic factors.
It also identifies classifying those individual optimal rates as part of the unresolved picture.
This would strengthen universal calibration guarantees by making forecasts competitive at each loss's own statistical scale rather than a single shared worst-case rate.
